evidence: The original helper `new RegExp(`${name}=([^;]*)`)` does substring-match `tp_session=` inside `__Host-tp_session=`, a real trap now that the PR introduced the prefixed name; 30322ef anchors it with `(?:^|;\s*)` and escapes the name.
guidance_note: When introducing a prefixed variant of an existing name (`__Host-tp_session`), sweep test helpers that match that name by substring.

evidence: `{ playgrounds: [] }` was defined in d1Catalog.ts, fileCatalog.ts and inline in memoryCatalog.ts; 30322ef lifts EMPTY_CATALOG into catalog.ts and imports it in all three.
guidance_note: When adding a third backend behind a seam, lift constants the existing backends each copy onto the seam module before adding a third copy.

evidence: The new D1 and R2 adapters had distinctive read-path mappings (null row -> empty, R2 null -> unknown version) with no tests; 30322ef adds d1Catalog/d1SessionStore/r2ArtifactStore tests with fakes.
guidance_note: Ship each new adapter with a contract test over a fake of the exact platform surface it touches, in the same PR.

evidence: Rebuilding stateless closures per fetch is a real but small cost, and the original comment had deliberately chosen per-request rebuild to avoid a mutable singleton; the fix added a module-level `let cachedHandler` that ignored `env` and directly produced F9. The packet has no measurement showing the allocation mattered.
guidance_note: When a reviewer's perf suggestion reverses a deliberate, commented trade-off, either push back with the original reasoning or design the cache keyed on its inputs from the first fix.

evidence: The header said `with a rollback path below` but the file held only CREATE statements; 30322ef replaces it with an explicit manual DROP block and states D1 migrations are forward-only.
guidance_note: Before claiming a property in a header comment (a rollback path below), check the file actually contains it.

evidence: Flag false positive: `await store.create(subject)` came from the original PR's async migration (hunk shows it pre-review) and 30322ef did not touch session.ts. The error was not silent but did reach the runtime's generic 500; the agent added one edge error boundary in worker.ts fetch instead of a local try/catch, which is the sounder single place.
guidance_note: When making a seam async and remote, check that each runtime entry point has an error boundary before shipping the first review round.

evidence: Flag false positive: the logout tests predate review and 30322ef did not change them. The PR added a SECURE cookie name but tested logout only under INSECURE; e4d943f adds the `__Host-tp_session=;` Max-Age=0 Secure assertion.
guidance_note: When a policy value (secure vs insecure) changes a derived name, run every existing route test under both policy values.

evidence: Flag false positive: the `as CatalogDoc` cast was original; 30322ef only swapped EMPTY for EMPTY_CATALOG on that file. The reviewer admits it already failed loudly, so the problem is the error message, not correctness. The fix in e4d943f guarded only the outer shape, which led to F11 and then F13.
guidance_note: When validating persisted input at a boundary, validate to every depth the function dereferences in the same change, not just the outer shape.

evidence: 30322ef's `handlerFor(env)` returned `cachedHandler` regardless of `env`, a signature that lies about its input, which the reviewer flagged as temporal coupling (not a current bug). e4d943f keys the cache on `cached.env === env`, a different fix from the reviewer's rename/drop-param.
guidance_note: When memoizing a function of a parameter, key the memo on that parameter from the start so the signature stays honest.

evidence: Flag false positive: the whoami `await resolveIdentity` line was in the original PR. e4d943f's worker fetch try/catch turns any rejection into a 500 carrying its message, so the failure is not silent; the reviewer itself concedes the outer boundary catches it. A second catch-all in the handler would duplicate that boundary.

e4d943f's guard checked `Array.isArray(doc.playgrounds)` then mapped `p.session.tags` unchecked, so `[null]` still crashed cryptically against the comment's own 'clear message' promise; the agent admits 'my guard checks the outer array but not the elements'.
guidance_note: When adding a shape guard whose stated purpose is a clear message, test it with malformed input at every level the function walks (outer, element, nested field).

evidence: Flag false positive: `required(env, name: keyof Env)` was in the original PR, unchanged by e4d943f. `keyof Env` admits the R2Bucket/D1Database keys, which always throw; 3c7d1c6 narrows to a RequiredEnvKey union.
guidance_note: Type a lookup helper's key parameter as only the keys whose value type it handles, not `keyof` the whole record.

evidence: 3c7d1c6 added `const p = entry as Playground` after checking only object+session, so `session: {}` passed and later crashed in summarize at `turns[0]`; 632f036 adds the non-empty `turns` check (one of the reviewer's two options) and reasonably declines a full leaf validator.
guidance_note: When validating persisted elements, check every invariant downstream code destructures (here non-empty `turns`), not just the field the migration touches.

evidence: Flag false positive: 632f036 changed only catalog.ts and its test; readCookie and cookies.test.ts were original PR code. The codec tests covered only bare names while serializeCookie tests covered `__Host-`, a real gap fixed in 1bde0c1.
guidance_note: When a PR adds a new name shape to a codec, test both directions (serialize and read) with that shape.

evidence: Flag false positive: the d1Catalog.ts header comment is original PR text. `carrying-cost` is a real token in the project's law set (cited elsewhere in this same batch); the reviewer was checking against its narrower charter.

Flag false positive: the `wrangler secret put ... or the [vars] table` message is visible in the original `required` (F12/F4 hunks), not introduced by 632f036. Offering [vars] for GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET steers operators toward committing a secret; 1bde0c1 makes the message per-category.
guidance_note: When writing operator guidance for secrets, give the secret-only mechanism per key rather than one message listing both mechanisms.

evidence: Flag false positive: frontDoorRouter tests are original PR code. A Fetch `Request`'s `.url` is always a parsed absolute URL, so the reviewer's 'not a url' input cannot be built as a Request; the test would cover an unrepresentable state.

Flag false positive: deploy-cloudflare.md is original PR text untouched by 632f036. The doc comment already said 'the two origins are told apart by the Host header' and curl showed `-H 'Host: ...'`, so the gap was small; a one-line clarification was a cheap, fair answer.

narrative: A large Cloudflare deploy PR that drew new advisory findings every round, mostly on original code the reviewer had not reached earlier. The costly thread was hydrateStoredDoc validation: each fix guarded one level deeper than the last (outer shape, then element, then turns), costing two follow-up findings and making round 3 (F13 only) entirely avoidable. The per-isolate cache added for a perf nit (F4) introduced an env-ignoring signature that F9 then flagged. Pushbacks on F10, F15 and F17 were well-founded.
guidance_observations: Boundary validation was grown one level per review round; writing the malformed-input table (outer, element, nested invariant) before the first fix would have closed the chain in one round.
Most ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags here are false positives: the reviewer re-scoped across rounds and raised issues on untouched original code.

evidence: The seed used `Subject('github:1')`, so only the prompt carried a payload; since `Subject` does not normalize, author escaping had no independent test. e245475 seeds `<script>alert(2)</script>` and asserts its escaped form, mutation-verified.
guidance_note: In an adversarial test matrix, give every attacker-controlled field the threat model names its own distinct hostile payload.

evidence: The 404 checked only `default-src 'none'` while the threat model claims full CSP on error paths. The choice to accept was right, but e245475 added only connect-src and nosniff while writing a comment claiming 'SAME thoroughness', which F3 caught.
guidance_note: When asked to make two paths assert the same thing, assert through one shared helper rather than copying a subset.

evidence: e245475's error path asserts 3 of the success path's 7 checks (missing form-action, base-uri, no 'self', no http) under a comment saying 'SAME thoroughness'. 585422d extracts `expectSealedCsp` used by both paths instead of copying assertions.
guidance_note: When the reviewer says 'match the success path', share the success path's assertion helper instead of hand-picking directives.

evidence: Flag false positive: the V2 cookie test is original code; e245475 changed only the seed, V4 and V6 assertions. `__Host-` requires `Path=/` and the posture test omitted it.
guidance_note: When asserting a spec-defined cookie prefix, assert every attribute that spec requires (Secure, Path=/, no Domain).

evidence: Flag false positive: the threat-model doc text is original and e245475 touched only the test file. The agent confirmed against types.ts that no `title` field exists.
guidance_note: When a security doc lists fields, check each one against the actual types before publishing.

narrative: A threat-model and adversarial-test PR. Round 0's error-path CSP fix was partial and carried an overclaiming 'same thoroughness' comment, which round 1 caught as F3. Round 1 also raised two findings unrelated to fixes, so the round would have happened anyway. Round 2 approved with no findings.
guidance_observations: A fix that writes a comment asserting parity ('SAME thoroughness') should make that parity structural (a shared helper) in the same commit, or the comment becomes the next finding.

evidence: `harden(await dispatch(request))` lets a throw bypass the seal, contradicting invariant #6's 'every branch'. The agent correctly pointed out that the reviewer's option (a), catch-seal-rethrow, discards the sealed response, and instead made the handler total, returning `harden(json({error}, 500))`.
guidance_note: When copying the content handler's 'single exit' seal pattern, copy its totality (a catch that returns a sealed error) along with it.

narrative: A small hardening PR with one real finding: the seal did not cover thrown errors. The agent rejected the reviewer's incoherent catch-and-rethrow option and made the handler total, which round 1 approved cleanly.

evidence: Appending CREATE TABLE reports to an already-applied 0001_init.sql would be skipped by D1's filename-tracked migrations; 76caba4 moves it into 0002_reports.sql and reverts the 0001 edit.
guidance_note: Never edit an existing migration file to add schema; add a new numbered migration.

evidence: The TOCTOU window needs a playground delete, and the Catalog interface has none (create/append/get/list), so it is unreachable. Documenting the assumption was the reviewer's own first option. The cited no-mode-explosion is the wrong token for 'no transaction for an unreachable case', which is carrying-cost.
`requireString` rejected only '' so a direct POST of '   ' passed while only the client trimmed; 76caba4 trims at the server boundary, rejects empty, and stores the trimmed value, with tests.
guidance_note: When the client normalizes input before submit, apply the same normalization at the server boundary rather than relying on the client.

evidence: Flag false positive: 76caba4 did not touch reportStore.ts; hydrateReportsDoc is original PR code whose comment claims it 'Mirrors the catalog's hydrateStoredDoc exactly' while omitting the per-element check the catalog had gained in PR #36. e7b58cd adds it.
guidance_note: When writing a function documented as mirroring an existing one, diff it against the original and carry over every check, including ones added during that original's review.

evidence: Flag false positive: 76caba4 only repointed the migration filename in this comment; the race and its KNOWN LIMITATION note were original. The race is real, and the agent kept the documented trade-off but corrected the comment to say it is reachable at the edge, unlike the write-free catalog. Accepting it at near-zero launch volume is defensible.
guidance_note: When documenting an inherited trade-off for a new store, check that the original's reason for accepting it (no edge writes) still holds for the new one.

evidence: Flag false positive: `readonly catalog: Catalog` is original code; e7b58cd touched only report storage. The comment claimed 'takes the read surface and nothing more' while the type granted writes; 9e80394 adds a CatalogReader and has Catalog extend it.
guidance_note: When a comment states a dependency is read-only, express it as a narrowed interface type in the same change.

evidence: Flag false positive: the integration test is original PR code. The reviewer itself says 'this is not a correctness gap' and that no list endpoint exists yet; durability is covered by the ReportStore contract test.

Flag false positive: 9e80394 touched reportService/catalog types, not d1ReportStore.ts. This repeats F5 against the comment e7b58cd had already made honest, and the reviewer restates the documented trade-off; declining further action was right.

narrative: A moderation-report PR. No finding was caused by an earlier fix: every ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag lands on original code the reviewer reached in a later round, or repeats an accepted trade-off (F8 repeats F5). Fixes were sound. F4 is a cross-PR repeat of the element-validation gap fixed in PR #36's hydrateStoredDoc.
guidance_observations: The report store was written as a 'mirror' of the catalog seam but missed hardening the catalog gained during PR #36's review; re-reading the mirrored module's current version would have prevented F4.

evidence: The reviewer's claim that escapeHtml is a 'pure no-op' after encodeURIComponent is false (encodeURIComponent leaves `'` intact), and dropping it would diverge from playgroundPages.playHref's byte-identical, documented idiom. The agent kept the code and added a short rationale comment.

Flag false positive: e0c1345 only added a comment in adminPages.ts; app.test.ts is original. The filename did misrepresent its scope, but a structural makeApp wiring test would duplicate integration coverage, so renaming (the reviewer's second option) was right.
guidance_note: Name a test file after the unit it actually tests.

evidence: Flag false positive: the two-store wiring is original PR code untouched by e0c1345. Two separate `makeMemoryReportStore()` instances behind intake and review contradict production wiring; edcf05a shares one.
guidance_note: When threading a new dependency into test fixtures, share the instances production shares instead of constructing a fresh one at each new call site.

evidence: Flag false positive: same original wiring as F3, in server.test.ts, untouched by e0c1345; edcf05a hoists one reportStore.
guidance_note: After fixing a wiring pattern in one fixture, grep for every other fixture that constructs the same pair.

evidence: Flag false positive: edcf05a changed only test files; the sessionId-keyed Map predates this PR, and this PR only narrowed its input to listed playgrounds. The reviewer concedes current code guarantees uniqueness; a per-read guard would enforce a write-time invariant at a read boundary.

narrative: An unlist/review-queue PR. No finding traces to an earlier fix: every ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag sits on original code or pre-existing catalog logic. The agent correctly declined the wrong 'no-op double-encoding' cure while documenting the idiom, and declined a speculative read-path uniqueness guard.
guidance_observations: Two findings (F3, F4) were the same fixture-wiring mistake in two files; constructing the new dependency once per fixture would have avoided both.
